chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amer, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muqatil ibn Sulayman. He said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Musa (peace be upon him) ascended to Tur and spoke privately with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, he said: O my Lord! Show me Your treasures. He said: O Musa! My treasure is that when I will a thing, I say to it "Be!" and it is.

key_terms.كن فيكون: Kun fa-yakun - 'Be! and it is', the divine creative command

ai.seo_question: What did God say to Prophet Musa when he asked to see His treasures?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates an exchange between Prophet Musa (AS) and God on Mount Tur. When Musa asked to see God's treasures, God responded that His treasure is not a physical storehouse but rather His infinite creative power, expressed through the divine command 'Kun fa-yakun' (Be! and it is). This reflects the Quranic concept of God's creative will, where existence flows directly from His command. The original audience would have understood this as a profound lesson about divine self-sufficiency and the nature of God's power, which needs no intermediary or means.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Muqatil b. Sulayman. He said:

Abu `Abdillah (as) said: When Musa (as) climbed Tur and his Lord whispered to him, he said: O Lord! Show me your treasure. He said: O Musa! Surely, My treasure is that, when I will a thing, I say to it “be!” and it is.
